changes.current_line: Recover failed payments automatically with smart retries.
changes.change: Recover failed payments and retries automatically. For studio operators, start with an export of your own failed renewals so you can see how many lost members never meant to leave.
changes.why: Only the failed-renewal data drew a response from the customer, and their own wording, 'failed payments and retries' and 'members who never meant to leave', is sharper than our current line.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: Stop leading with the global opener for regional operators, such as a few US studios and Canadian sites. Open with the customer's own churn split instead.
changes.why: The global-scale opener did not fit a customer with a handful of regional sites, and the failed-renewal data was the only part that got a response.

changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: Do not claim in-store or front-desk coverage for a customer until a live demo runs in their own studio management software or a phase-two date is set. Describe the front desk in plain words before using the term 'unified commerce'.
changes.why: The customer heard 'unified commerce' as hardware, and the front-desk flow ran through a partner integration that was only shown in the partner's demo, not in their setup.

changes.change: For finance buyers: run a failed-renewal data session with the controller before any proposal goes to them, and include failed-renewal numbers and exit terms in a finance-facing version of the proposal.
changes.why: The controller held the paper for two weeks, asked for the customer's own spreadsheet, and signed four days after the data session, so the signer needed finance-specific proof rather than the head of digital's view.
